scripts.radio:
Habari zenu, this is Kenya on Record. Nairobi taps are set to run dry once again. This week, the Nairobi City Water and Sewerage Company announced a three-day complete shutdown of the main supply line to allow for pipeline maintenance. While routine maintenance is an accepted part of utility management, the lived reality for Nairobi residents tells a much heavier story.

For households across Kasarani, Lang'ata, Dagoretti, and Eastlands, three days of dry taps is not a minor inconvenience. It is a costly disruption. The moment an official shutdown notice is circulated, private water bowsers and vendors instantly inflate their prices, turning an essential public service into an extortionate commodity. Families are forced to dig deep into their pockets just to cook and access basic sanitation.

We must ask Nairobi Water and the County Government: what safeguards have been instituted to protect citizens from price-gouging cartels during scheduled works? Where are the emergency relief bowsers for public clinics, schools, and informal settlements? Infrastructure maintenance must not continually penalize the taxpayer while enriching private profiteers. Take note of your meter readings before the shutdown begins, monitor what your ward representatives are doing, and hold your utility provider accountable.

Kwa ufupi: Kampuni ya Maji ya Nairobi imetangaza kufunga mabomba kwa siku tatu kwa ajili ya ukarabati. Hakikisha umehifadhi maji ya kutosha mapema, piga picha mita yako, na uwe mwangalifu na walanguzi wanaopandisha bei za maji kiholela wakati huu.
scripts.voice_note: Habari zenu, this is Kenya on Record with a heads-up for everyone in Nairobi. Nairobi Water has announced a three-day maintenance shutdown that will cut supply across several estates. We all know what happens next: the taps dry up and the water bowser business immediately doubles or triples prices. Here is what we need to do. First, harvest and store enough water for domestic use right now before pressure falls off. Second, if you rely on vendors, agree on prices beforehand so you are not exploited in an emergency. Lastly, check and document your water meter reading today before the shutdown starts, so you aren't billed for air when the lines are repressurized. Tuwe macho, share this note with your estate group, and plan ahead.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: Nairobi Water shutdown is here. Store water early and record your meter reading today. Do not let vendors overcharge you for essential public water.
scripts.reels: Three full days without a single drop from the tap. Nairobi Water calls it scheduled maintenance. But on the ground, it means families paying triple to private water vendors just to survive the week. Maintenance is necessary, but leaving citizens at the mercy of informal cartels is unacceptable. Store your water today, check your meter, and demand proper contingency plans from City Hall.
